'''''Goeppertia sanderiana''''' is a [[species]] of plant belonging to the genus [[Goeppertia]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Marantaceae]]. It is native to Peru and has been introduced to El Salvador and Honduras.<ref name="POWO">{{Cite web |date=2024 |title=''Goeppertia sanderiana'' (Sander) Borchs. & S.Suárez |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:77130042-1 |access-date=2024-08-31 |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=[[Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew]] |language=en}}</ref> It is a very common ornemental plant used in homes because of its beautiful foliage. It belongs to one of the groups in the ''Goeppertia'' genus called the [[Ornata Group]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Kennedy |first=Helen |date=1995 |title=Will the real Calathea ornata stand up?. Heliconia Society International Bulletin. 7 (3): 12–16. |url=https://www.heliconia.org/_files/ugd/ef1aa2_66186af9be254c7f91b66f0220f67161.pdf}}</ref>

== Description ==
[[File:Calathea ornata 'Sanderiana' Kalatea 2010-08-01 02.jpg|thumb|Inflorescence of ''Goeppertia sanderiana''|left]]''Goeppertia sanderiana'' has dark green leaves with a pink, white striped pattern on the upper side of the leaf.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=1912 |title=Flora of Peru |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/bibliography/42246 |journal=Publication. Field Museum of Natural History. Botanical series |publisher=Field Museum of Natural History. |via=BHL}}</ref> This pattern disappears as the plant matures and is all green when mature. The bottom side of the leaf is purple throughout the plant's life. The inflorescence of ''Goeppertia sanderiana'' is similar to [[Goeppertia elliptica]], [[Goeppertia bantae]] or [[Calathea monstera]].<ref name=":0" />





== A confusion... ==
Goeppertia sanderiana is often sold as Pin-stripe Calathea or [[Goeppertia ornata|Calathea ornata]]. While this species do exist, the plant that is sold around the world is Goeppertia sanderiana (or [[Goeppertia majestica]]). The real [[Goeppertia ornata]] is a very rare striped pattern species of Goeppertia native to Venezuela and Colombia and disappeared from cultivation some time prior to the mid-1990s.<ref name=":0" />
